decisions.label: Negotiate a Political Opening
decisions.summary: Open a paid, reversible legal-status negotiation; no automatic transfer of power.

decisions.label: Individual Prisoner Review
decisions.summary: Review opposition detention case by case; release is not an automatic party accession.

decisions.label: Offer an Autonomy Accord
decisions.summary: Domestic KDP response and territorial definition required; no automatic March1970 success.

decisions.label: Constitutional Revision Conference
decisions.summary: Reopen a selected institutional policy at real political and administrative cost; never replay national investments.

decisions.label: Negotiate a National Progressive Front
decisions.summary: ICP may accept, refuse or seek guarantees; coalition participation does not make it governing subparty.

decisions.label: Regional Leadership Contest
decisions.summary: Convene the Regional Command to settle the presidency among eligible party leaders. The incumbent retains office until a successor is selected.

decisions.label: Appoint a Continuity Cabinet
decisions.summary: Preserve existing eligible successors including Tariq Aziz. A Tariq Aziz government retains shared Baath, economy, defence and foreign programmes; no forced Bakr/Saddam-only dead end.

decisions.label: Negotiate the Division of Offices
decisions.summary: Risk a contested leadership settlement; existing leader system resolves the outcome.

decisions.label: Offer a Friendship Treaty
decisions.summary: Soviet acceptance required; arms, loan or advisory terms selected separately. No free faction membership.

decisions.label: Offer a Syrian Union Conference
decisions.summary: Both governments must consent. Shared institutions and leadership terms are negotiated, with no automatic annexation.

decisions.label: Implement the Agreed Succession
decisions.summary: Install only an eligible agreed successor. Bakr programme suspends; irreversible national gains remain.

decisions.label: Review Policy toward Iran
decisions.summary: Available only after an observed Iranian regime change or explicit RP dossier; choose negotiation, deterrence or a separate war decision.

decisions.label: Request a Gulf Credit Line
decisions.summary: Lender chooses amount and terms; matching lender debit, Iraqi treasury credit and Iraqi debt increase only on acceptance.

decisions.label: Repay a Negotiated Credit Tranche
decisions.summary: Repayment equals min(selected tranche, actual debt, available treasury); no money or debt creation.

decisions.label: Offer a Conditional Amnesty
decisions.summary: Opposition chooses whether to accept. No automatic coup immunity or power transfer.

decisions.label: Submit the Transition Charter
decisions.summary: A constitutional vote may fail; success permits civilian accession through MD politics, not arbitrary party support replacement.

decisions.label: Convene an Arab Socialist Leadership Council
decisions.summary: Bring the party leadership together to nominate a living, eligible executive and settle the direction of the Arab socialist programme.

decisions.label: Offer an Arab Development Compact
decisions.summary: Egypt or Syria may refuse; one initiator, defined payer and recipient, no duplicated factory reward.

decisions.label: Offer an Approved Support Package
decisions.summary: Existing eligible recipient and native support ledger required; no invented militia or automatic foreign war.

decisions.label: Convene a Union Negotiation
decisions.summary: Every participating player consents to institutions, finance and military authority. No automatic territorial merger.

decisions.label: Elect the Party Secretariat
decisions.summary: Convene the Communist Party congress to choose an eligible secretary and settle the leadership of its political programme.

decisions.label: Submit Front Conditions
decisions.summary: Negotiate legal rights and ministries; front membership does not by itself activate governing-party programmes.

decisions.label: Open Federal Negotiations
decisions.summary: KDP/PUK and provincial representatives respond; no free cores, territorial transfer or Kurdish loyalty variable invented.

decisions.label: Request a Party and Technical Exchange
decisions.summary: Soviet response required; scholarship and adviser costs are explicit.

decisions.label: Review Continued Front Participation
decisions.summary: Review the Communist Party’s participation in the governing Front. Withdrawal ends the coalition agreement without transferring the presidency.

decisions.label: Offer a Minimum Democratic Charter
decisions.summary: Other domestic parties accept or reject separately; no automatic all-party alliance.

decisions.label: Hold a Leadership Renewal Vote
decisions.summary: Use the leadership registry. A departing secretary loses this active programme, while earned progress survives.

decisions.label: Hold a Contested Parliamentary Election
decisions.summary: Hold a parliamentary election among the legal parties. The result determines which party forms the next government.

decisions.label: Request Parliamentary Credit Approval
decisions.summary: Accepted external loans use matching treasury/debt changes; refusal leaves domestic policy playable.

decisions.label: Review the Cabinet Programme
decisions.summary: A later coalition can revise selected funded policy slots without replaying old rewards.

decisions.label: Offer a Hashemite Cooperation Treaty
decisions.summary: Jordan can refuse. No automatic federation, common monarch or annexation.

decisions.label: Offer a Commercial Partnership
decisions.summary: Negotiated payer, recipient and construction capacity; foreign refusal has no domestic veto.

decisions.label: Offer a Costed Cooperation Treaty
decisions.summary: USSR, a Western state or regional partner may accept/refuse. No automatic bloc membership, foreign base or loan.

decisions.label: Offer a Navigation and Border Conference
decisions.summary: Iran accepts/refuses/revises. Existing border remains until explicit agreed implementation; no automatic treaty or peace.

decisions.label: Offer a Border Incident Review
decisions.summary: Both states receive a response opportunity; no automatic escalation or forced stand-down.

decisions.label: Offer a Syrian Cooperation Conference
decisions.summary: Syria controls its response; union, transit and defence terms remain separate decisions.

decisions.label: Offer a Kuwait Finance and Navigation Conference
decisions.summary: No automatic claim, core or annexation. Kuwait decides finance and border terms.

decisions.label: Convene a Regional Reconciliation Conference
decisions.summary: Each invitee may refuse. Accepted terms do not automatically bind uninvolved players.

decisions.label: Request a Regional Debt Review
decisions.summary: Creditor approval required. Debt changes only by actual agreed payment or explicit creditor write-off.

decisions.label: Review Active Treaty Obligations
decisions.summary: A revision needs counterpart response where required. No reward replay or automatic diplomatic immunity.

decisions.label: Convene the KDP Leadership Council
decisions.summary: Convene the Kurdish leadership to choose a living, eligible executive and agree the party’s negotiating position.

decisions.label: Convene Kirkuk Status Talks
decisions.summary: No automatic ethnic transfer, core, annexation or resource ownership. All status changes need a constitutional agreement.

decisions.label: Offer a Regional Cooperation Pact
decisions.summary: KDP may refuse. No forced merger of movements or automatic national government.

decisions.label: Call a Federal Convention
decisions.summary: Arab and Kurdish parties negotiate constitutional authority and revenue. No automatic approval.

decisions.label: Select a Political Executive
decisions.summary: Select an eligible political executive to direct Dawa’s organisation and government programme.

decisions.label: Offer a Non-Interference Accord
decisions.summary: Iran must accept; agreement protects recipient control and does not transfer state authority.

decisions.label: Offer a Border and Non-Interference Treaty
decisions.summary: Iran may refuse; no automatic border transfer or end to an active war.

decisions.label: Request a Published Reconstruction Package
decisions.summary: Actual treasury/debt effects and force permissions require accepted terms.

decisions.label: Reconstitute the IIP Leadership
decisions.summary: Convene eligible party organisers to elect a political executive and reconstitute the Islamic Party leadership.

decisions.label: Offer an Arab Civilian Partnership
decisions.summary: Partner accepts/refuses. No automatic sectarian bloc or foreign military access.

decisions.label: Submit Revised Concession Terms
decisions.summary: Foreign counterpart may accept/refuse; no concession benefit before accepted terms.

decisions.label: Review the Oil Market Position
decisions.summary: Read current world-price/sanctions state. No unilateral increase of the world oil price.

decisions.label: Renegotiate an Export Contract
decisions.summary: Review the terms of an existing oil contract and seek a replacement agreement. The current contract remains subject to its own terms until replaced.

decisions.label: Review Funded Industrial Projects
decisions.summary: Pending projects retain a frozen invoice. Capacity/control failure delivers no benefit and charges no treasury.

decisions.label: Request an Industrial Credit Agreement
decisions.summary: Accepted lender debit and matching Iraqi treasury/debt; ordinary domestic investment remains possible if refused.

decisions.label: Repay a Foreign Credit Tranche
decisions.summary: Repay an outstanding foreign credit from the treasury. Payment cannot exceed the recorded obligation or the funds available.

decisions.label: Reallocate the Next Investment Round
decisions.summary: Select one current future-investment policy. Existing factories remain; no second grant from repeating review.

decisions.label: Offer a River Management Conference
decisions.summary: Turkey and Syria respond separately. No free water resource, new dam or automatic treaty.

decisions.label: Review Education and Service Coverage
decisions.summary: Reads existing native education/law data. Does not reset literacy each time government changes.

decisions.label: Review Social Coverage and Funding
decisions.summary: Replace the selected coverage policy; permanent literacy and built infrastructure remain.

decisions.label: Request Soviet Advisers
decisions.summary: Counterpart accepts/refuses; advice has cost and duration. No automatic division, licence or research tech.

decisions.label: Fund a Readiness Cycle
decisions.summary: Fund 90 days of readiness: organization +4%, organization recovery +4%, army personnel costs +4%. Cost: 0.5% of GDP; 180-day cooldown.

decisions.label: Request Crisis Mediation
decisions.summary: Ask an eligible government to mediate the current dispute. A settlement requires the parties’ agreement.

decisions.label: Authorize a Specific War Proposal
decisions.summary: Present the current territorial dispute to the cabinet and authorize a specific war proposal. An authorization does not itself declare war.

decisions.label: Request a Postwar Debt Conference
decisions.summary: Creditors can refuse. No automatic Gulf write-off, claim onKuwait or new war.

decisions.label: Request a Sanctions Review
decisions.summary: Seek a review of the sanctions currently imposed on Iraq. Relief depends on the governments responsible for those measures.

decisions.label: Review Remaining Emergency Measures
decisions.summary: End active war-policy costs and bonuses after peace; veteran support remains a real budget choice.

decisions.label: Review the Eastern Balance
decisions.summary: Expose actual Iranian stability, war status, owned Khuzestan and the Iraqi northern burden. Never manufacture an Iranian revolution or a loyal Arab uprising.

decisions.label: Repudiate the Border Settlement
decisions.summary: Repudiate the existing border agreement with Iran. Its reciprocal benefits end and the unresolved river dispute returns.

decisions.label: Exploit Iranian Disarray
decisions.summary: Commit 1% of annual GDP to exploiting a current Iranian civil war or stability below 40%. Planning Speed: +10% for 120 days. Available once.
decisions.eligibility: country_exists = PER; PER = { OR = { has_civil_war = yes has_stability < 0.40 } }; NOT = { has_country_flag = COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_disarray_used }

decisions.label: Request Gulf War Credit
decisions.summary: Select a real Gulf creditor. Terms, amount, Iraqi debt, repayment and creditor treasury debit require recipient acceptance. Refusal cannot block the ultimatum. No free oil, loans or divisions.

decisions.label: Negotiate a Wartime Supply Contract
decisions.summary: Approach an eligible arms supplier for a wartime delivery. Equipment, funding and delivery depend on the supplier’s agreement and available stocks.

decisions.label: Launch the Khuzestan Offensive
decisions.summary: Commit 2% of annual GDP within the first 30 days of war with Iran. Choose a short offensive or a sustained campaign; both increase operational costs and impose an army personnel bill that continues after an early peace.
decisions.eligibility: has_war_with = PER; earned iran_launch_campaign; first-war window open; no COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_opening_used flag; invoice affordable

decisions.label: Fund a Renewed Offensive
decisions.summary: After at least 90 days of war and the end of the opening campaign, commit 3% of annual GDP. Attack against Iran: +5% for 60 days; Supply Consumption and Army Fuel Consumption: +12%. Army personnel costs rise for 90 days. Cooldown: 180 days.
decisions.eligibility: has_war_with = PER;90continuous war days; NOT any opening/followup idea or followup bill; frozen invoice affordable

decisions.label: Revise the War Aims
decisions.summary: Choose continued prosecution, a new offensive or a limited negotiated offer. Iran may refuse settlement; no forced peace, claim removal or free debt relief. Ending the war suspends emergency bonuses and attrition, while fixed-duration bills still expire on their original dates.

decisions.label: Deliver a Pending Programme
decisions.summary: Available from start when any completed focus has a pending delivery. Select one pending item; recheck its exact government, live contract, ownership/control, native capacity and frozen invoice. Execute its same once-only delivery guard. Failed retry charges nothing. No new quote or duplicated reward.
decisions.eligibility: IRQ; at least one COLDWAR_IRQ_<focus>_pending flag; chosen focus not yet implemented

decisions.label: Organize the Western Outlook
decisions.summary: Support an existing party of the Western outlook through a political campaign. Cost: 55 Political Power. Party Support and Outlook Support: +3 points before normalization. Cooldown: 180 days. The campaign does not change the government.

decisions.label: Organize the Emerging Outlook
decisions.summary: Support an existing party of the Emerging outlook through a political campaign. Cost: 55 Political Power. Party Support and Outlook Support: +3 points before normalization. Cooldown: 180 days. The campaign does not change the government.

decisions.label: Organize the Non-Aligned Outlook
decisions.summary: Support an existing party of the Non-Aligned outlook through a political campaign. Cost: 55 Political Power. Party Support and Outlook Support: +3 points before normalization. Cooldown: 180 days. The campaign does not change the government.

decisions.label: Organize the Nationalist Outlook
decisions.summary: Support an existing party of the Nationalist outlook through a political campaign. Cost: 55 Political Power. Party Support and Outlook Support: +3 points before normalization. Cooldown: 180 days. The campaign does not change the government.

decisions.label: The Communist Question
decisions.summary: Determine whether the Communist Party seeks legal participation in the Front or organises an independent opposition. The incumbent government retains office.

decisions.label: Convene a Constitutional Conference
decisions.summary: Choose the current constitutional settlement. Ratification costs 1% of GDP and replaces incompatible programme authority.

decisions.label: Negotiate the Front Labour Charter
decisions.summary: Independent workplace representation supports industrial cooperation while requiring funded social commitments.

decisions.label: Mobilize the Party Organizations
decisions.summary: Coordinate the party organizations through the executive, with a funded administrative commitment.

decisions.label: Review the Army Priority
decisions.summary: Redistribute the current military priority between the Guard and the regular army. The review costs 1% of GDP.

decisions.label: Negotiate a Second Advisory Mission
decisions.summary: Invite a French or British advisory mission on agreed terms. The partner can refuse; accepted advisers require Iraqi funding.

decisions.label: Review the Rural Credit Priority
decisions.summary: Redistribute future rural credit between cooperative machinery and smallholder guarantees. Review costs 1% of GDP; existing farms and completed investments remain.

decisions.label: Review the Oil Revenue Priority
decisions.summary: Reallocate the next planning round between export revenue and non-oil development. Review costs 1% of GDP; completed investment remains in place.

decisions.label: Negotiate the Northern Revenue Settlement
decisions.summary: Negotiate revenue-sharing or central administration with local guarantees. Ratification costs 2% of GDP; regional governments control their response.

starting_spirits.label: The July State
starting_spirits.description: The 1968 regime rests on the Revolutionary Command Council, party organization and coercive institutions. State consolidation conceals factional insecurity.
starting_spirits.treatment: Baath institutional choices replace this spirit; suspend it when Baath leaves government. Never turn the later Saddam personality cult into a January 1970 fact.

starting_spirits.label: An Unsettled Northern Question
starting_spirits.description: The Kurdish war and unresolved demands for autonomy strain Baghdad. The March 1970 accord is still a negotiation, not a starting achievement.
starting_spirits.treatment: A fulfilled autonomy contract reduces the national burden; negotiated federal settlement replaces it. Local insecurity is not simulated with resistance on Iraqi cores.

starting_spirits.label: Oil Beneath Foreign Concessions
starting_spirits.description: The Iraq Petroleum Company concession system and disputes over production constrain control over oil revenue despite the 1961 expropriation of undeveloped concession areas.
starting_spirits.treatment: Nationalization or a renegotiated concession replaces this modifier. Oil remains finite map resources; no second fictional oil income system.

starting_spirits.label: The Unfinished Agrarian Reform
starting_spirits.description: Unequal landholding, weak delivery of reform, rural credit shortages and limited irrigation hinder agriculture and encourage migration.
starting_spirits.treatment: Agricultural credit, tenure and irrigation milestones remove separate penalties. Agriculture input values follow MD calculations, not literal historical output percentages.

starting_spirits.label: A Narrow Base of Skills
starting_spirits.description: Low literacy and uneven access to education restrict the capacity to absorb complex civilian and military technology.
starting_spirits.native_system: Native MD literacy/education dynamic modifier; proposed literacy_rate = 0.35, calibration pending historical evidence. No extra research penalty.
starting_spirits.treatment: Initialize the missing1970 literacy input once, then use update_literacy_rate. Native education already calculates research, skills and costs. Proposed35% is a balance placeholder, not a verified historical statistic.

starting_spirits.label: Patronage and Parallel Chains of Command
starting_spirits.description: Personal networks and competing civilian, security and military authorities obstruct administration. This is not a claim that every Iraqi institution was equally dysfunctional.
starting_spirits.treatment: Civil service audit and command reforms address distinct components; no duplicated native corruption-tier penalty or free blanket corruption removal.

starting_spirits.label: The Shatt al-Arab Dispute
starting_spirits.description: The border and navigation dispute with Iran worsened in 1969. It is a diplomatic problem with potential military costs, not an unavoidable future war.
starting_spirits.treatment: Accepted and fulfilled navigation/border settlement replaces this. Neither the 1975 settlement nor the 1980 invasion is applied at game start.

layout.font: Native hoi_16mbs UbuntuBold16 atlas and glyph advances; all titles <=143px inside native147px text region

programme_rules.stability_cap_scope: min(sum positive active policy contributions, 0.15) + sum negative active policy contributions. Original situation spirits are separate; negative choices remain fully effective above the positive cap.
programme_rules.reconciliation: Recompute group variables from earned, selected, currently eligible packages; variables are derived caches, not re-awarded one-time effects.
programme_rules.policy_selection: The original18-focus programmes use two separate selected-policy slots. Iran has two independent explicit choices: Short War versus Sustained War, and Equal Citizenship versus Central State Rule. Its river and Khuzestan demand lanes are compatible. Descendants follow their selected slot; revisions never replay original effects.
programme_rules.funding: Frozen invoice, pay on valid delivery. Explicit Iraq1970 price proposals use stated GDPshares; native2000 helper prices remain comparison data, not automatic charges. No deposit/refund. Unfunded delivery exposes a start-accessible retry with zero reward; dependent focuses require delivered predecessors. Early oil/agriculture/factory projects are optional funded spurs.
programme_rules.price_calibration: Native7.5-billion factory price equals229% of the existing Iraqi1970 GDP3.281, so copying it wholesale would obstruct the campaign. GDPshare project quotes are NEW balance proposals using existing treasury/construction APIs; engine budget calibration remains untested. Office-only project gives no free power plant.
programme_rules.party_availability: Branches remain visible and become unavailable without governing-party/leader qualification; dynamic programmes detach and reattach. Never promise runtime branch disappearance.
programme_rules.iran_campaign: The Khuzestan claim and conquest goal are unilateral focus rewards, not permission requests to Iran. Declaration is a player action. One-use opening ideas target PER; no permanent global attack bonus is granted. First-war timing, automatic180day attrition, settlement repudiation and paid decision transactions need new authored integration.
programme_rules.khuzestan_integration: A separate alternate-history integration continuation can grant an Iraqi core after730continuous days of actual ownership/control, peace with Iran, infrastructure3, compliance60+, resistance below15 and a6%GDP invoice. The selected civic/central costs continue while holding the state. No re-awards or removal of other countries cores.

COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_opening_offensive.label: The Southern Offensive
COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_opening_offensive.description: Prepared attacks against Iranian forces have a short operational window. Fuel and supply costs affect the entire Iraqi army. Peace ends the advantage; it never restarts.

COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_sustained_offensive.label: A Prepared Iranian Campaign
COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_sustained_offensive.description: A larger reserve supports a longer opening operation, with a smaller attack advantage and continuing logistical costs.

COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_mobilization_bill.label: The Mobilization Bill
COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_mobilization_bill.description: Personnel and transport obligations remain payable even if the initial campaign ends early.

COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_disarray_assessment.label: Intelligence on Iranian Disarray
COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_disarray_assessment.description: A funded assessment of an actual Iranian political crisis accelerates planning. It does not weaken Iranian units or guarantee local cooperation.

COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_attrition_bill.label: A War Beyond the First Campaign
COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_attrition_bill.description: After 180 continuous days at war with Iran, replacement, transport and political burdens grow. This burden ends at peace.

COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_followup_offensive.label: A Renewed Southern Offensive
COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_followup_offensive.description: Another paid offensive offers a smaller advantage against Iran, at higher logistical strain. It cannot overlap the opening or another renewed offensive.

COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_followup_bill.label: Replacement and Transport Contracts
COLDWAR_IRQ_iran_followup_bill.description: The renewed offensive leaves ninety days of personnel obligations, including after an early peace.

legacy_decisions.label: Review Funded Industrial Projects
legacy_decisions.summary: Pending projects retain a frozen invoice. Capacity/control failure delivers no benefit and charges no treasury.

legacy_decisions.label: Reallocate the Next Investment Round
legacy_decisions.summary: Select one current future-investment policy. Existing factories remain; no second grant from repeating review.

legacy_decisions.label: Review Social Coverage and Funding
legacy_decisions.summary: Replace the selected coverage policy; permanent literacy and built infrastructure remain.
